title: The Tilting Vessel
text:
Confucius once visited the ancestral temple of Duke Huan of Lu and noticed a strange vessel set at an angle. He asked the temple keeper what it was. The keeper told him it was a vessel kept at the right side of the seat as a warning.

Confucius said he had heard of such vessels: when empty they tilt, when filled halfway they stand upright, and when full they overturn. He told his disciples to pour water into it. They did. Halfway full, it stood straight. When they filled it to the top, it tipped over and spilled. When it was empty, it leaned again.

Confucius sighed and said: "Ah! Is there anything that is full and does not overturn?"

His disciple Zilu asked whether there was a way to hold on to fullness. Confucius said that intelligence should be guarded with an air of simplicity, great achievement with modesty, courage with caution, and wealth with humility. This, he said, is the way to draw water out before the vessel overflows.
lesson: Success is the moment of greatest risk, because it tempts you to keep filling. When things go best, add humility and caution on purpose instead of more ambition.
